verdict.rationale: Shopify documents public APIs for driving the platform programmatically: the Admin GraphQL API for extending the admin, and the Storefront API for products, carts and checkout. It also documents scoped access-token authentication, quarterly API versioning, and a GraphiQL explorer for running queries and mutations. Community posts criticize the API's design and report tier-gated access, but none concretely shows the API failing to work as documented. Missing for 10: hands-on corroboration that the API works as documented, and a machine-readable spec (OpenAPI paths return 404, though the APIs are GraphQL).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The Admin API lets you build apps and integrations that extend and enhance the Shopify admin.
The API offers a full range of commerce options making it possible for customers to view products and collections, add products to a cart, and check out.
Your code obtains an access token scoped to the permissions it needs.
Shopify releases new API versions on a predictable quarterly schedule, giving you time to adopt changes before older versions are retired.
